answer: Each agent receives a unique kernel credential only after a small, nonrefundable stake is locked and its account completes a trellis of independently verified tasks over time. Rewards depend on sustained, cross-checked contributions, so creating many identities does not multiply influence: each new account must fund its own stake and earn its own history. An attacker pays capital and verification effort for every sybil, while risking the stake if identities coordinate or fail checks. A new island of accounts cannot bootstrap trust from its own endorsements.
